why_it_works: Top PwC/ULI 2026 market; top spot in both overall real estate and homebuilding prospects; major projected job gains; strong scale/liquidity for 1-4 unit exits and financing.
key_evidence: PwC ranks DFW #1 overall and says it also leads homebuilding prospects; Moody's projects leading job gains.
main_risk: Texas affordability pressure and broader Sun Belt supply competition can compress near-term rent growth in some submarkets.
best_fit: Investors prioritizing liquidity, appreciation durability, and broad neighborhood choice.

why_it_works: PwC highlights stronger job growth forecast than DFW; Arbor still shows positive multifamily rent growth in 2026; diversified knowledge-economy demand fits duplex/fourplex rentals.
key_evidence: PwC names Raleigh/Durham among Southeast markets with stronger job growth forecasts than DFW; Arbor shows +1.6% multifamily rent growth through Mar 2026.
main_risk: Price competition and selective new supply can limit immediate cash-on-cash returns.
best_fit: Long-hold investors wanting growth plus relatively resilient renter demand.

why_it_works: Supply-disciplined big metro with strong rent/occupancy performance and more attainable 2-4 unit stock than coastal gateways.
key_evidence: PwC says Chicago made a sizable upward move in 2026 rankings; Arbor shows +1.6% multifamily rent growth; Steadily cites 95.6% occupancy and construction pipeline of only ~1.4% of inventory.
main_risk: Illinois taxes/regulation and slower long-run population story versus Sun Belt growth metros.
best_fit: Investors focused on house-hacking, small multifamily cash flow, and dense neighborhood demand.

why_it_works: Still a top job-growth market; demand kept pace unusually well with supply wave; attractive if buying after concessions rather than at peak pricing.
key_evidence: PwC says Charlotte has one of the strongest Southeast job growth forecasts; Arbor shows +2.1% multifamily rent growth; Steadily notes >30,000 recent net jobs and demand/absorption keeping up with heavy deliveries.
main_risk: Near-term oversupply/concessions mean you must buy right and underwrite softer year-one rents.
best_fit: Investors comfortable buying into temporary softness for medium-term rebound.

why_it_works: PwC still ranks Houston near the top nationally; large projected job gains and deep transaction market support long-term small-property liquidity.
key_evidence: PwC says Houston slipped only slightly to #5 and follows DFW closely on projected job gains.
main_risk: Texas insurance/climate exposure and some Sun Belt supply pressure.
best_fit: Buyers wanting scale, relative affordability vs. other top metros, and strong employment engines.

why_it_works: Overlooked market with favorable income-growth outlook and low relative business costs; can work well for small multifamily where basis matters more than headline migration.
key_evidence: PwC says Pittsburgh rose more than 10 spots and highlights strong per-capita income growth/outlook due to low relative business costs.
main_risk: Lower liquidity and slower population momentum than the top Sun Belt / Research Triangle markets.
best_fit: Investors seeking stable basis and less speculative pricing.

why_it_works: Balanced Midwest growth story with steady rent growth, strong absorption, and relatively reasonable entry costs for duplex-triplex-fourplex deals.
key_evidence: Steadily cites 3-4% rent growth, >6,000 units of recent absorption, and a slowing construction pipeline; vacancies remain manageable relative to growth.
main_risk: Some recent new supply means investors still need submarket discipline.
best_fit: Cash-flow oriented investors who still want a real growth metro, not a pure tertiary bet.

why_it_works: Midwest rent growth remained positive; affordability supports small-balance deal economics better than expensive growth metros.
key_evidence: Arbor lists Cleveland among Midwest rent-growth leaders at +1.6% through Mar 2026; Forbes notes affordable I-90 corridor markets were among strongest SFR growth clusters.
main_risk: Weaker long-run population growth caps appreciation upside.
best_fit: Investors prioritizing basis and yield over headline appreciation.
